subject: SLO playbook scope + prompt bundle request (post-call)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T15:12:00Z
Subject: SLO playbook scope + prompt bundle request (post-call)

Beth — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and asks so we can scope the performance qualification run and avoid back-and-forth: 

Summary of EdgeCommerce workload (from call):
- Feature: real-time conversational product recommender integrated into checkout; outputs average ~60 tokens, streaming to UI.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 120 concurrent active users; expected steady throughput ~200 requests/s with burst windows up to 420 rps for ~30s.
- Latency sensitivity: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) matters for UX; streaming-first-chunk under 200ms is your baseline.

Redwood initial SLOs (proposal) — please flag if these mismatch what you promised customers:
- Completion latency p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 700ms (for 60-token streaming responses)
- Time-to-first-byte (first streaming chunk) p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms
- Sustained throughput target: 200 rps steady-state with correct tail-latency bounds; peak burst handling to 420 rps for burst tolerance testing
- Concurrency handling: maintain SLOs at 120 concurrent sessions; spike tests to 400 concurrency to validate graceful degradation

Benchmark methodology we propose (high level):
1) Preparation: Edge to deliver a prompt bundle (representative distribution) + traffic profile spreadsheet (arrival distribution, token length distro).
2) Warm-up: 30-minute gradual warmup to populate caches, KV layers and steady batching patterns.
3) Steady-state run: 45 minutes at target throughput for metrics collection.
4) Burst tests: short 30s–2min bursts to 420 rps to observe routing fallbacks and autoscaling.
5) Streaming validation: measure TTFB and per-chunk arrival time; capture aggregated token/sec and chunk tail latencies.

Measurement definitions (we will publish exact spec in the harness):
- Request latency: measured server-side from recv(request) to last byte, reported p50/p90/p95/p99
- TTFB (first streaming chunk): time from recv(request) to first non-empty chunk delivered
- Throughput: completed requests/sec and tokens/sec (system-side accounting)
- Reproducibility: use fixed random seed where generation is stochastic, pin model binary + quantization profile, record hardware SKU and driver/kernel versions

Immediate asks for you (EdgeCommerce):
- Share a prompt bundle (json) that covers your 90th percentile conversational turn types (we referenced an example attachment name below).
- Traffic profile spreadsheet (arrival distro, token length histogram, expected concurrency curve).
- If you have an internal test token or sandbox dataset we can use to avoid touching prod connectors, share access details.

Attachments included: edge_prompt_bundle_v1.json (placeholder), edge_traffic_profile_202611.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
- You deliver prompt bundle + profile by EOD Tue (2026-11-30).
- Redwood schedules a 2-hour canary window next week (we'll share a calendaring poll once we have artifacts).
- Marissa will own the harness run and will follow up on tooling and measurement spec.

Thanks — want to make sure the performance spec is what you expect before we lock dates.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Beth Carter <beth@edgecommerce.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: perf-team <perf-team@edgecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO playbook scope + prompt bundle request (post-call)

Rishi — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we send the bundle: 

1) Latency: the team wanted p95 tail no higher than ~600ms for typical queries. Your proposed 700ms is acceptable for initial run but we'd like to aim for 600ms as the target after tuning.

2) Streaming: time-to-first-chunk target is 150ms at p95 for our EU customers; we're okay to validate US region first.

3) Workload: our median response length is 55 tokens, 95th at 140 tokens. The traffic_profile spreadsheet will include the token length histogram and arrival shape (we use a Weibull for burst modeling).

4) Test dataset: we'll provide edge_prompt_bundle_v1.json and a sandbox API key scoped to a non-prod environment. Expect an SFTP with files and a short readme by EOD Monday (2026-11-30).

Small ask: can you confirm the harness will record both server-side and client-observed latencies? We need both for client SLAs.

I'll loop in our infra perf owner if needed.

—Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Platform Engineering — EdgeCommerce
beth@edgecommerce.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T18:10:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO playbook scope + prompt bundle request (post-call)

Perfect — thanks Beth. Confirmations below: 
- We'll treat the 600ms p95 as the engineering target for post-tuning; initial acceptance window for qualification will be 700ms pending tuning actions.
- Harness will capture both server-side service metrics (server recv->lastByte) and simulated client-observed (client send->first/last chunk) — we'll provide the mapping table in the harness README.
- We'll run in US region first per your note; if you want EU parity testing we'll replicate after the initial pass (extra lead time for infra placement).

Marissa: can you draft the concrete measurement spec (JSON) and a lightweight k6 script we can run in the Canary? Put it in the repo and share the link back to Beth. Also call out the warm-up and seed rules.

Beth — expect calendar poll from me for windows on Wed/Thu next week. If you can share the SFTP details and prompt bundle per your timeline that will let Marissa stand up the canary config tonight.

—Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Beth Carter <beth@edgecommerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO playbook scope + prompt bundle request (post-call)

Adding the concrete checklist from engineering side so everyone is aligned: 

Engineering checklist (what Redwood will deliver for the canary run):
- Measurement spec JSON (attached in repo) with exact metric names (request_latency_ms, ttfb_ms, tokens_per_sec, model_quant_profile)
- k6 load script with client-side timers and headers to emulate streaming; warm-up 30m, steady 45m, bursts as described
- Canary run log bundle and perf dashboard link (Grafana) + raw CSV export for post-analysis
- Repro rules: pinned model artifact id, quantization flags, HW SKU recorded, fixed RNG seed for deterministic sampling where used

Risk notes:
- If prompt bundle contains very long-context examples (>> 1k tokens) we'll need to split tests or increase infra; call this out in the profile.
- Third-party integrations (DB lookups or product catalog calls) must be stubbed in the sandbox to avoid external tails.

I'll upload the measurement-spec.json and the k6 script to the harness repo and post links here within 2 hours. Once Beth confirms the files are accessible, we'll schedule the 2-hour canary window and run an initial smoke pass.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
